results.label: this tree ships the M112 trading-window rule (the committed parent does not, and that absence is this probe's control)
with the routine complete and no window selected the desk is clear — so every refusal below is the window
a window that cannot contain the trader’s local time produces the SAME kind of stop the personal guardrails produce
and the breach names the rule rather than a generic stand-down
the state is published on the daily object every consumer already reads, beside the breaches
the message is the module sentence, so the UI and the refusal cannot drift apart
results.detail: No personal stop. 3 entries remain under the preselected 3-entry cap. This is not market/setup approval.

results.label: the entry-admission path REFUSES it: 409, the guardrail code, and the operation never runs (no trade is written)
and an override reason cannot open it, because the window sets can_override false
the refusal is AUDITED with the window in the snapshot, so the trader can see which boundary stopped which attempt
a desk whose routine is incomplete is stopped by its own rule, and the window is not needed to explain it
without a window that stop is overridable with a stated reason — the routine is a stop the trader may answer for
with the window outside as well, BOTH rules are in the breach list — the window appends, it never replaces
and the window is the stricter rule: an overridable routine stop becomes non-overridable once the boundary is crossed
so the stated reason no longer admits the entry, and the refusal still names the routine as well as the window
a window that CONTAINS the local time blocks nothing at all — it is a boundary, not a permission
and the same call that was refused a moment ago now admits the entry
the state is DERIVED from the stored window and the clock on every read: the same row is outside at 13:15 local and inside the wrap at 23:00 local
and the wrapped window is ONE boundary: `inside` at 01:30 the far side of midnight, and the end minute is OUTSIDE it
and reading it again at the frozen clock refuses again — nothing was cached and nothing decayed
clearing the window (four NULLs) blocks nothing, and the daily is what it was before any window existed
the scan path turns the same state into NO TRADE on the candidate, with the market read preserved beside it
and it says WHY in the candidate’s own no-trade list, prefixed as a personal guardrail rather than a market fact
the permission it publishes is the window’s own stop, so a client renders the personal state rather than re-deriving it

detail.message: No personal stop. 3 entries remain under the preselected 3-entry cap. This is not market/setup approval.

results.label: and the action permission that accompanies a recorded action keeps its scope note, so nothing here is broker permission
the desk playlist publishes the window’s own stop rather than a second opinion about it: the SAME input is allowed when the clock is inside and refused when it is outside
and it SAYS it: the window adds exactly one block-level guard carrying the module’s sentence, and the headline names it too

detail.headline: EURUSD 15m: no directional read. The higher timeframe has not decided which side of the range it wants.

results.label: with no window selected the playlist is measurably what it was: no window sentence anywhere in it and permission unchanged
a window authored in a zone the trader has since changed is `unavailable`, and BOTH zones are named in the sentence
and it blocks: an unreadable window refuses the entry rather than opening the gate the trader asked to close
reading the state twice is idempotent: the same breaches, the same window, no counter and no journal row moved
the only tables two reads touch are the guardrail audit tables the existing observe path already writes (and the rowid counter beside them)
no journal row, no account row, no setting and no trade moved: the window is read, not stored
